subproblem.title: Caccioppoli inequality for C^1 weak solutions of constant-coefficient Legendre-elliptic systems
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, L := L(R^n, R^l), lam > 0 and Lam real. There is a constant C >= 0 with the following property. Let A be a continuous bilinear form on L with A[P][P] >= lam ||P||^2 and |A[P][Q]| <= Lam ||P|| ||Q|| for all P, Q in L. Let V : R^n -> R^l, y in R^n, rho > 0 and c in R^l. Assume V is C^1 on B_{2 rho}(y), and the integral over R^n of A[DV(x)][Dzeta(x)] is 0 for every C^1 compactly supported zeta : R^n -> R^l with tsupport zeta in B_{2 rho}(y). Then the lower Lebesgue integral over B_rho(y) of ||DV||^2 is at most (C / rho^2) times the lower Lebesgue integral over B_{2 rho}(y) of |V - c|^2 (values in [0, infinity]; the right side may be infinite).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (lam Lam : ℝ), 0 < lam → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (A : (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] ℝ) (V : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (y : Rn n) (ρ : ℝ) (c : Rn ℓ), (∀ P : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, lam * ‖P‖ ^ 2 ≤ A P P) → (∀ P Q : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, |A P Q| ≤ Lam * ‖P‖ * ‖Q‖) → 0 < ρ → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 V (ball y (2 * ρ)) → (∀ ζ : Rn n → Rn ℓ, ContDiff ℝ 1 ζ → HasCompactSupport ζ → tsupport ζ ⊆ ball y (2 * ρ) → ∫ x, A (fderiv ℝ V x) (fderiv ℝ ζ x) = 0) → ∫⁻ x in ball y ρ, ‖fderiv ℝ V x‖ₑ ^ 2 ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C / ρ ^ 2) * ∫⁻ x in ball y (2 * ρ), ‖V x - c‖ₑ ^ 2
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (Caccioppoli inequality for constant coefficients). It is stated with lower Lebesgue integrals in [0, infinity] (Lean: ∫⁻ with ‖.‖ₑ ^ 2, where ‖v‖ₑ = ofReal ‖v‖), because the right side may be infinite.
Notation. L := L(R^n, R^l) with the operator norm. For v in R^l and a linear form p on R^n, v (x) p denotes the element h -> p(h) v of L; its operator norm is |v| ||p||. In Lean this is ContinuousLinearMap.smulRight p v, with norm ‖p‖ * ‖v‖.
1. The constant. Let psi(s) := smoothTransition((3 - s)/2), where Real.smoothTransition : R -> R is Mathlib's C^infinity function with values in [0,1] that equals 0 on (-infinity, 0] and 1 on [1, infinity). Then psi is C^infinity, 0 <= psi <= 1, psi = 1 on (-infinity, 1], and psi = 0 on [3, infinity). The derivative psi' is continuous and vanishes outside [1, 3], so c_psi := sup |psi'| is finite. Put C := 64 c_psi^2 Lam^2 / lam^2 >= 0. It depends only on lam and Lam, since psi is fixed once and for all.
2. Cutoff. Fix A, V, y, rho > 0 and c as in the statement, and put eta(x) := psi(|x - y|^2 / rho^2). Then eta is C^infinity on R^n, 0 <= eta <= 1, and eta = 1 on B_rho(y). Also eta(x) = 0 whenever |x - y|^2 >= 3 rho^2, so tsupport eta is contained in closedBall(y, sqrt(3) rho), which is a compact subset of B_{2 rho}(y). Moreover Deta(x)h = psi'(|x - y|^2/rho^2) * 2<x - y, h>/rho^2. Hence ||Deta(x)|| <= 2 c_psi |x - y| / rho^2 <= 2 sqrt(3) c_psi / rho <= 4 c_psi / rho when |x - y| <= sqrt(3) rho, and Deta(x) = 0 otherwise. So ||Deta||^2 <= 16 c_psi^2 / rho^2 everywhere.
3. Test function. Let zeta(x) := eta(x)^2 (V(x) - c). On the open set B_{2 rho}(y), zeta is C^1 as a product of C^1 maps. On the open set R^n \ tsupport eta, zeta is identically 0. These two open sets cover R^n, so zeta is C^1 on R^n. Its tsupport is contained in tsupport eta, hence compact and contained in B_{2 rho}(y). By hypothesis, the integral of A[DV(x)][Dzeta(x)] dx is 0. On B_{2 rho}(y), Dzeta = eta^2 DV + 2 eta (V - c) (x) Deta. Outside tsupport eta, Dzeta = 0 because zeta vanishes near such points. (The values of DV outside B_{2 rho}(y) play no role.)
4. Expansion. For x in B_{2 rho}(y), bilinearity gives A[DV][Dzeta] = eta^2 A[DV][DV] + 2 eta A[DV][(V - c) (x) Deta]. For x outside tsupport eta, both sides are 0. Extend the following functions by 0 outside tsupport eta: f1 := eta^2 A[DV][DV], f2 := eta A[DV][(V - c) (x) Deta], g1 := eta^2 ||DV||^2, g2 := eta ||DV|| |V - c| ||Deta||, g3 := |V - c|^2 ||Deta||^2. Each is continuous on R^n: it is continuous on B_{2 rho}(y), where V is C^1, it is 0 on the open set R^n \ tsupport eta, and these sets cover R^n. Each has support in the compact set tsupport eta, so each is integrable. Therefore 0 = integral of f1 + 2 (integral of f2).
5. Absorption. By the Legendre condition, lam (integral of g1) <= integral of f1 = -2 (integral of f2) <= 2 (integral of |f2|) <= 2 Lam (integral of g2). The last step uses |A[P][Q]| <= Lam ||P|| ||Q|| and ||(V - c) (x) Deta|| = |V - c| ||Deta||. Young's inequality 2 Lam a b <= (lam/2) a^2 + (2 Lam^2/lam) b^2, with a := eta ||DV|| and b := |V - c| ||Deta||, gives 2 Lam g2 <= (lam/2) g1 + (2 Lam^2/lam) g3 pointwise. Hence lam (integral of g1) <= (lam/2)(integral of g1) + (2 Lam^2/lam)(integral of g3). The integral of g1 is finite, so the integral of g1 is at most (4 Lam^2/lam^2) times the integral of g3.
6. Lower integrals. Since eta = 1 on B_rho(y), the lower integral over B_rho(y) of ||DV||_e^2 is at most the lower integral over R^n of ofReal(g1). The latter equals ofReal(integral of g1), because g1 is integrable and nonnegative. By step 2, and since tsupport eta is contained in B_{2 rho}(y), we have g3 <= (16 c_psi^2/rho^2) |V - c|^2 1_{B_{2 rho}(y)} pointwise. So ofReal(integral of g3) = lower integral of ofReal(g3) <= ofReal(16 c_psi^2/rho^2) times the lower integral over B_{2 rho}(y) of ||V - c||_e^2. Combining with step 5, in [0, infinity]: lower integral over B_rho(y) of ||DV||_e^2 <= ofReal(4 Lam^2/lam^2) ofReal(integral of g3) <= ofReal(4 Lam^2/lam^2) ofReal(16 c_psi^2/rho^2) times the lower integral over B_{2 rho}(y) of ||V - c||_e^2. This equals ofReal(C/rho^2) times the same lower integral, because ofReal is multiplicative on nonnegative reals. Every step is an inequality between products in [0, infinity] with the convention 0 * infinity = 0, so the chain is valid even when the last integral is infinite. QED
proof_key_steps: fixed cutoff profile psi built from Real.smoothTransition; C := 64 c_psi^2 Lam^2 / lam^2
eta = psi(|x-y|^2/rho^2): eta = 1 on B_rho(y), tsupport eta in B_{2rho}(y), ||Deta|| <= 4 c_psi/rho
zeta := eta^2 (V - c) is C^1 on R^n (glue B_{2rho}(y) with the complement of tsupport eta) and admissible
expand A[DV][Dzeta] by bilinearity; all integrands are continuous with compact support
Legendre + bound + Young, then absorb the finite term: integral of eta^2 ||DV||^2 <= (4 Lam^2/lam^2) integral of |V-c|^2 ||Deta||^2
pass to lower integrals in [0, infinity] using eta = 1 on B_rho(y) and ||Deta||^2 <= 16 c_psi^2/rho^2

audit.reason: The lower-integral contract matches the prose, including a potentially infinite right-hand side. The cutoff makes the test globally C1 despite only local regularity of V. All absorption integrals are finite; coercivity, the bilinear bound, and Young's inequality give the stated constant. Passing to ENNReal preserves validity even when a coefficient is zero and the outer integral is infinite.
